children.title: Affine-Scaling Predictor Directions
children.top_down_role: Direction families emphasizing progress toward the solution boundary.

assumptions_latex: The affine predictor sets the target complementarity to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine-scaling direction solves \(A\Delta x=0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=-Xs\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible affine-scaling predictor obtained by setting the complementarity target to zero.

source_refs.locator: Affine-Scaling Steps p. 128

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a strictly positive primal-dual feasible point, compute the affine-scaling predictor from \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=0,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=-Xs.\] Determine the largest \(\alpha_{\max}^{\mathrm{aff}}\in(0,1]\) for which \(x+\alpha\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}\ge0\) and \(s+\alpha\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\ge0\). The direction is the Newton predictor for the formal target \(Xs=0\); a practical iterate uses a smaller positive step to remain strictly interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine predictor is the feasible Newton direction toward zero complementarity, truncated to preserve positivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Scaling Predictor Directions

source_witnesses.locator: Affine-Scaling Steps p. 128

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Gap Reduction Along the Affine Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate complementarity under a common feasible affine-scaling step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the feasible affine direction satisfies \(A\Delta x=0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=-Xs\), then \(\Delta x^{\mathsf T}\Delta s=0\) and, for every common step length \(\alpha\), \[(x+\alpha\Delta x)^{\mathsf T}(s+\alpha\Delta s)=(1-\alpha)x^{\mathsf T}s.\] Consequently, every positivity-preserving common step with \(0<\alpha<1\) reduces the duality gap by the factor \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common feasible affine step reduces aggregate complementarity exactly by one minus the step length.
assumptions_latex: The affine direction satisfies the feasible zero-target Newton equations.
The primal and slack updates use the same step length \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x+\alpha\Delta x)^{\mathsf T}(s+\alpha\Delta s)=(1-\alpha)x^{\mathsf T}s.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Gap Reduction Along the Affine Direction

children.title: Combined Primal-Dual Directions
children.top_down_role: Direction families coupling progress and centering components.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Primal-Dual Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible Newton directions combining affine complementarity reduction with a centering target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a strictly positive primal-dual feasible point, choose \(0<\sigma<1\), set \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\), and compute \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) from \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu\mathbf1-Xs.\] The term \(-Xs\) supplies the affine progress component and \(\sigma\mu\mathbf1\) supplies the centering component. Choose \(\alpha>0\) so that \(x+\alpha\Delta x>0\), \(s+\alpha\Delta s>0\), and the updated point satisfies the algorithm's destination-neighborhood condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined primal-dual direction uses one feasible Newton system to blend affine complementarity reduction with a positive centering target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined direction solves \(A\Delta x=0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu\mathbf1-Xs\).

notation.meaning: centering weight in the combined direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Gap Contraction of a Combined Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate complementarity under a common feasible centering-and-progress step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the combined direction satisfies \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu\mathbf1-Xs,\] where \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), then \(\Delta x^{\mathsf T}\Delta s=0\) and, for every common step length \(\alpha\), \[(x+\alpha\Delta x)^{\mathsf T}(s+\alpha\Delta s)=\bigl(1-\alpha(1-\sigma)\bigr)x^{\mathsf T}s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common feasible combined step contracts the duality gap by one minus the step length times one minus the centering weight.
assumptions_latex: The primal and slack updates use the same step length \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x+\alpha\Delta x)^{\mathsf T}(s+\alpha\Delta s)=\bigl(1-\alpha(1-\sigma)\bigr)x^{\mathsf T}s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible correction canceling the componentwise quadratic product generated by an affine predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}})\) be a feasible affine predictor. A second-order correction satisfies \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{cor}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}.\] Its complementarity right-hand side cancels the affine move's componentwise quadratic product. A centered corrector instead uses \(\sigma\mu\mathbf1-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order correction preserves linearized feasibility and cancels the affine predictor’s quadratic complementarity error, optionally while adding a central target.
assumptions_latex: A feasible affine predictor has been computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of the affine primal direction

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Complementarity Correction
Higher-Order Correction Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal power-series corrections for the primal-dual complementarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a feasible primal-dual point satisfy \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(x,s>0\). For a prescribed first-order complementarity target \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), define corrections by \(A\Delta x^{(k)}=0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{(k)}+\Delta s^{(k)}=0\) for every \(k\ge1\), with \[S\Delta x^{(1)}+X\Delta s^{(1)}=h-Xs,\qquad S\Delta x^{(k)}+X\Delta s^{(k)}=-\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\Delta X^{(j)}\Delta s^{(k-j)},\quad k\ge2.\] Then the truncated direction \((\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha^k\Delta x^{(k)},\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha^k\Delta y^{(k)},\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha^k\Delta s^{(k)})\) cancels complementarity-series coefficients through order \(p\), leaving a residual of order \(O(\alpha^{p+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive feasible corrections cancel the quadratic and higher product terms arising when a primal-dual Newton direction is expanded along a trajectory.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X(\alpha)s(\alpha)=Xs+\alpha(h-Xs)+O(\alpha^{p+1})\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of the kth primal correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Centrality Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation criterion for the Euclidean primal-dual neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\) and suppose \(\|Xs-\mu e\|_2\le\theta\mu\). Let a feasible Newton direction satisfy \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu e-Xs.\] For \(0<\alpha\le1\), set \((x^+,y^+,s^+)=(x,y,s)+\alpha(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) and \(\mu^+=(1-\alpha+\alpha\sigma)\mu\). If \(x^+,s^+>0\) and \[\|(1-\alpha)(Xs-\mu e)+\alpha^2\Delta X\Delta s\|_2\le\theta\mu^+,\] then \(\|X^+s^+-\mu^+e\|_2\le\theta\mu^+\); hence the updated point remains in the same central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible Newton step preserves the Euclidean central neighborhood whenever positivity holds and its exact post-step complementarity residual satisfies the neighborhood bound.
assumptions_latex: The current point is strictly feasible and belongs to the stated neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^+,y^+,s^+)\in\mathcal N_2(\theta)\).

notation.meaning: Strictly feasible points satisfying the Euclidean centrality inequality.

Diagonal matrices formed from x and s.

children.title: Centrality Recovery
children.top_down_role: Analysis families for returning from a prediction region to a central region.

knowledge_statements.title: Centrality Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full centering-Newton recovery in the Euclidean neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,y,s)\) be strictly feasible and let \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). The pure centering direction is defined by \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\mu e-Xs.\] Feasibility implies \(\Delta x^{\mathsf T}\Delta s=0\). Consequently, for the full step \((x^+,y^+,s^+)=(x,y,s)+(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\), one has \(\mu^+=\mu\) and \[X^+s^+-\mu e=\Delta X\Delta s.\] Thus, if \(x^+,s^+>0\) and \(\|\Delta X\Delta s\|_2\le\theta\mu\), the full centering step recovers membership in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full centering step returns to the Euclidean central neighborhood when positivity holds and the remaining second-order complementarity product is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and the Newton system is solvable.

children.title: Interiority Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Structural controls preserving membership in the barrier domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Interiority Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fraction-to-the-boundary safeguard for primal and dual slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x,s>0\), a direction \((\Delta x,\Delta s)\), and \(0<\eta<1\), define \[\alpha_x=\min\left\{1,\eta\min_{i:\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i}\right\},\qquad \alpha_s=\min\left\{1,\eta\min_{i:\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i}\right\},\] where the minimum over an empty index set is \(+\infty\), and set \(\alpha=\min\{\alpha_x,\alpha_s\}\). Output \(x^+=x+\alpha\Delta x\) and \(s^+=s+\alpha\Delta s\). Then every component of \(x^+\) and \(s^+\) is positive, so the update remains in the logarithmic-barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fraction-to-the-boundary rule shortens a direction enough to keep every primal variable and dual slack strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+\alpha\Delta x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and \(s+\alpha\Delta s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).

notation.meaning: Primal and dual admissible step lengths.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Boundary of the Fraction-to-the-Boundary Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The maximal boundary step need not preserve strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z>0\) and direction \(d\), define \[\bar\alpha(z,d)=\min_{i:d_i<0}\frac{-z_i}{d_i},\] with \(\bar\alpha=+\infty\) if no component decreases. Then \(z+\alpha d>0\) for every \(0\le\alpha<\bar\alpha\). If \(\bar\alpha<\infty\), at least one component is zero at \(\alpha=\bar\alpha\). Thus a fraction factor below one preserves strict positivity, whereas taking the limiting step can reach the barrier-domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximal nonnegative step can make a limiting component zero, so an unconditional strict-interiority safeguard uses a fraction strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\alpha<\bar\alpha\Rightarrow z+\alpha d>0;\quad \bar\alpha<\infty\Rightarrow z+\bar\alpha d\notin\mathbb R_{++}^n.

notation.meaning: limiting step to the coordinate boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Short-Step and MTY Predictor-Corrector Path-Following Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded comparison of two primal-dual LP path-following regimes. The short-step complexity claim is stated only relative to the unextracted comparison theorem referenced by the source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In short-step primal-dual path following, a conservative centering parameter \(\sigma<1\), chosen sufficiently close to \(1\), permits the full step \(\alpha=1\) while preserving membership in a restrictive \(\mathcal N_2\) neighborhood. The analogue of the source's referenced path-following complexity result replaces \(n\) by \(n^{1/2}\) in that estimate. In the Mizuno--Todd--Ye predictor-corrector method, two nested neighborhoods \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{in}}\subset\mathcal N_{\mathrm{out}}\) are used. A predictor step begins in \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{in}}\), follows the affine-scaling direction obtained with \(\sigma=0\), and moves to the boundary of \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{out}}\). The alternating corrector step uses \(\sigma=1\) and \(\alpha=1\) to return the iterate to \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{in}}\). The resulting duality measures \(\mu_k\) converge superlinearly to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short-step path following uses a centering parameter slightly below one so that full steps remain in a restrictive central-path neighborhood. Relative to the complexity result referenced by the extract, its dimension dependence replaces n by the square root of n. The Mizuno–Todd–Ye method alternates an affine-scaling predictor from an inner neighborhood to the boundary of an outer neighborhood with a full corrector step back into the inner neighborhood; its duality measures converge superlinearly to zero.
assumptions_latex: The method is a primal-dual path-following method for linear programming, with duality measures \(\mu_k=x_k^Ts_k/n\).
In the short-step regime, \(\sigma<1\) is sufficiently close to \(1\) that \(\alpha=1\) preserves the prescribed restrictive \(\mathcal N_2\) neighborhood.
In the MTY regime, \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{in}}\subset\mathcal N_{\mathrm{out}}\) are nested \(\mathcal N_2\) neighborhoods, and the specified predictor and corrector steps alternate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The short-step analogue has \(n^{1/2}\) in place of \(n\) in the referenced complexity estimate, while the MTY sequence satisfies \(\mu_k\to0\) superlinearly.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Short-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained logarithmic-barrier short-step method in primal coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\), choose \(x^0>0\) with \(Ax^0=b\), a parameter \(t_0>0\), and a neighborhood threshold \(\beta\). At iteration \(k\), set \(t_{k+1}=(1+\delta/\sqrt n)t_k\). Compute the equality-constrained Newton direction \(d^k\) for \[\phi_{t_{k+1}}(x)=t_{k+1}c^{\mathsf T}x-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\] at \(x^k\), and take \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\). Choose fixed \(\delta>0\) and \(\beta<1\) so that the Newton decrement remains at most \(\beta\). Stop and output \(x^k\) when \(n/t_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the primal barrier parameter by a small relative amount, take one feasible Newton step, and stop when the barrier duality bound reaches the requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasible region has a strictly feasible point.
The initial Newton decrement for \(\phi_{t_0}\) is at most \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax^k=b\), \(x^k>0\), and termination occurs after \(O(\sqrt n\log(n/(t_0\varepsilon)))\) updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Short-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic-barrier short-step method in dual equality coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual problem \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s>0\}\), choose \(y^0\) with \(s^0=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^0>0\), a parameter \(t_0>0\), and threshold \(\beta\). Set \(t_{k+1}=(1+\delta/\sqrt n)t_k\), and let \(g_k=b-t_{k+1}^{-1}A(S^k)^{-1}e\) and \(H_k=-t_{k+1}^{-1}A(S^k)^{-2}A^{\mathsf T}\). Solve \(H_kd^k=-g_k\), set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+d^k\), and set \(s^{k+1}=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}\). Fixed sufficiently small \(\delta\) preserves the decrement bound \(\beta<1\). Stop when \(n/t_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the dual barrier parameter slightly and take one Newton step for the dual log-barrier while preserving positive slacks and a small decrement.
assumptions_latex: The dual feasible region has a strictly feasible point.
The initial dual Newton decrement is at most \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k=c\), \(s^k>0\), with \(O(\sqrt n\log(n/(t_0\varepsilon)))\) updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Short-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible short-step method in coupled primal-dual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\in\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) satisfying \(Ax^0=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0=c\), and \(x^0,s^0>0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\mu_k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k/n\) and \(\widehat\mu_k=(1-\delta/\sqrt n)\mu_k\). Solve \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S^k\Delta x+X^k\Delta s=\widehat\mu_ke-X^ks^k,\] and take the full update \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1},s^{k+1})=(x^k,y^k,s^k)+(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\). For sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\) and \(\theta\), the iterates remain in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\). Stop when \(n\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce average complementarity by a small relative amount and take one coupled feasible Newton step while maintaining a narrow central neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible initial point in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) is available.
\(\delta\) and \(\theta\) satisfy the standard short-step bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) after \(O(\sqrt n\log(n\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Newton Short-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step barrier update followed by one undamped Newton recentering step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) on \(\{x>0:Ax=b\}\), and let \(x^k\) have Newton decrement at most \(\beta<1\) for \(f_{t_k}(x)=t_kc^{\mathsf T}x+F(x)\). Set \(t_{k+1}=(1+\delta/\sqrt n)t_k\). Compute the equality-constrained Newton direction \(d^k\) from \[Ad^k=0,\qquad \nabla^2F(x^k)d^k+t_{k+1}c+\nabla F(x^k)+A^{\mathsf T}w^k=0,\] and take the full step \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\). For sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\), self-concordant Newton estimates give \(x^{k+1}>0\) and restore decrement at most \(\beta\). Stop when \(n/t_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each small barrier-parameter increase, one undamped feasible Newton step restores the prescribed centrality neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is strictly feasible and \(A\) has full row rank.
The initial decrement is at most \(\beta\).
\(\delta\) is within the short-step self-concordant bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}>0\), \(Ax^{k+1}=b\), and the Newton-decrement invariant is preserved.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine trial point and trial duality measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Notation for trial points along a primal-dual long-step search direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the current iterate $(x^k,\lambda^k,s^k)$ and direction $(\Delta x^k,\Delta\lambda^k,\Delta s^k)$, define, for a trial step length $\alpha$,
\[
(x^k(\alpha),\lambda^k(\alpha),s^k(\alpha))=(x^k,\lambda^k,s^k)+\alpha(\Delta x^k,\Delta\lambda^k,\Delta s^k),
\]
and
\[
\mu_k(\alpha)=\frac{x^k(\alpha)^Ts^k(\alpha)}{n}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial primal-dual point is obtained by moving alpha units along the current search direction. Its trial duality measure is the average complementarity product at that trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^k(\alpha)=z^k+\alpha\Delta z^k,\qquad \mu_k(\alpha)=x^k(\alpha)^Ts^k(\alpha)/n.

knowledge_statements.title: Wide-Neighborhood Long-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible long-step method using a componentwise centrality neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\gamma<1\) and define \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\) by strict feasibility and \(x_is_i\ge\gamma\mu\) for every \(i\), where \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). From a point in this neighborhood, choose \(0\le\sigma<1\) and solve \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=0,\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu e-Xs.\] Choose the largest safeguarded \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) for which the updated point belongs to \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\), then update all variables. Repeat until \(n\mu\le\varepsilon\). Permitting the full componentwise neighborhood allows larger target changes than a narrow Euclidean short-step neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A long-step method takes the largest safeguarded Newton step that preserves positive variables and a componentwise lower bound on complementarity.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible starting point lies in \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\in\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\) until \(n\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a strictly feasible iterate \((x,y,s)\) lie in a prescribed central neighborhood \(\mathcal N(\theta)\), with \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). For each \(\rho\) in a finite ordered trial set contained in \((0,1)\), solve \[A\Delta x(\rho)=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y(\rho)+\Delta s(\rho)=0,\qquad S\Delta x(\rho)+X\Delta s(\rho)=(1-\rho)\mu e-Xs.\] Select the largest trial \(\rho_k\) whose full candidate is positive and belongs to \(\mathcal N(\theta)\), and set \(\alpha_k=1\). If no full trial satisfies the prescribed acceptance floor, choose a safeguarded pair \((\rho_k,\alpha_k)\) with \(\rho_k\in(0,1)\) and \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) such that the damped candidate remains positive and belongs to \(\mathcal N(\theta)\). Accept \((x^+,y^+,s^+)=(x,y,s)+\alpha_k(\Delta x(\rho_k),\Delta y(\rho_k),\Delta s(\rho_k))\). Then feasibility implies \(\Delta x(\rho_k)^{\mathsf T}\Delta s(\rho_k)=0\), so \(\mu^+=(1-\alpha_k\rho_k)\mu\). Stop when \(n\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the largest tested complementarity reduction whose full Newton update remains positive and central; when a damped safeguard is needed, account for its step length in the achieved complementarity reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Mehrotra Predictor-Corrector Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard infeasible-start primal-dual LP predictor-corrector iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). At an iterate \((x,y,s)\) with \(x>0\) and \(s>0\), define \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s\), and \(\mu=x^Ts/n\). First solve \(A\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}=r_p\), \(A^T\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=r_d\), and \(S\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=-Xs\). Choose maximal affine step lengths in \([0,1]\) that preserve nonnegativity, define \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}=(x+\alpha_p^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}})^T(s+\alpha_d^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}})/n\), and set \(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3\). Using the same Newton coefficient matrix, compute the combined direction from \(A\Delta x=r_p\), \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=-Xs+\sigma\mu e-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\). Take fraction-to-boundary primal and dual steps and stop when the feasibility residuals and duality gap satisfy their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an affine predictor, use its predicted complementarity to choose a centering parameter, then reuse the Newton matrix for a centered second-order direction and take positivity-preserving steps.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The primal-dual Newton coefficient matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^+,y^+,s^+)=(x+\alpha_p\Delta x,\ y+\alpha_d\Delta y,\ s+\alpha_d\Delta s)\), where \(x^+>0\) and \(s^+>0\).

children.title: Multiple-Correction Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Correction Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated centrality corrections following one primal-dual predictor step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior iterate, compute a predictor direction and initialize its accepted trial direction as \(d^{(0)}\). For \(j=1,\ldots,k\), evaluate the trial complementarity products \((x+\alpha_p d_x^{(j-1)})\circ(s+\alpha_d d_s^{(j-1)})\), construct a correction right-hand side that moves these products toward a prescribed neighborhood of \(\mu^+e\), and solve the unchanged primal-dual Newton matrix for a correction \(q^{(j)}\). Set \(d^{(j)}=d^{(j-1)}+q^{(j)}\), retaining the correction only if it enlarges the admissible positivity-preserving step or improves the neighborhood measure. Output the trial point generated by the last retained direction; stop by residual and gap tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After one predictor, repeatedly reuse its Newton factorization to correct trial complementarity, retaining corrections that improve centrality or permit a longer safe step.
assumptions_latex: A central-path neighborhood and fraction-to-boundary rule are fixed.
Each correction uses the same nonsingular Newton coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{(k)}=d^{(0)}+\sum_{j=1}^{k}q^{(j)}\), and the accepted trial point remains strictly interior.

notation.meaning: Target average complementarity at the trial point.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Trajectory-Following Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order local approximation of the primal-dual central trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z(\mu)=(x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) satisfy the primal-dual central-path equations. At \(\mu_k>0\), differentiate those equations once and twice to compute \(z'_k\) and \(z''_k\). For a chosen \(\mu_{k+1}<\mu_k\), form the quadratic predictor \(\widehat z_{k+1}=z_k+h_kz'_k+\tfrac12h_k^2z''_k\), where \(h_k=\mu_{k+1}-\mu_k\). Reduce \(|h_k|\) until the predicted primal and dual variables are positive and satisfy the selected path neighborhood; optionally apply one Newton correction at \(\mu_{k+1}\). Output the corrected point and stop when its complementarity and feasibility residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiate the central-path equations twice, predict the next point with a quadratic trajectory model, restrict the step to preserve positivity, and optionally recenter.
assumptions_latex: The central-path Jacobian is nonsingular near \(\mu_k\).
The trajectory \(z(\mu)\) is twice differentiable locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z(\mu_k+h_k)=z_k+h_kz'_k+\tfrac12h_k^2z''_k+o(h_k^2)\).

notation.meaning: First and second path derivatives at the current parameter.

review_flags: Several inequivalent second-order trajectory algorithms exist.
A source is needed to identify the intended neighborhood and correction variant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic quadratic trajectory construction is plausible, but no source establishes that it is the intended second-order trajectory-following family or supports its neighborhood and correction rules.

children.title: Ordinary Central-Path Targets
children.top_down_role: Target-following structures based on the ordinary central path.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Central-Path Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted primal-dual central-path target for a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For \(\mu>0\), the ordinary primal-dual central-path target is the strictly feasible triple \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) satisfying \[Ax(\mu)=b,\qquad A^Ty(\mu)+s(\mu)=c,\qquad X(\mu)s(\mu)=\mu e,\qquad x(\mu)>0,\ s(\mu)>0.\] Equivalently, \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Under strict primal-dual feasibility and full row rank of \(A\), this triple exists and is unique for each \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each positive parameter, the ordinary central-path target is the unique strictly feasible primal-dual point whose coordinatewise complementarity products all equal that parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The primal and dual standard-form LPs are strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax(\mu)=b\), \(A^Ty(\mu)+s(\mu)=c\), and \(X(\mu)s(\mu)=\mu e\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix formed from the primal central-path point.

source_refs.locator: The Central Path p. 7

source_witnesses.locator: The Central Path p. 7

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap certificate intrinsic to an ordinary central-path target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every ordinary central-path target, \[c^{\mathsf T}x(\mu)-b^{\mathsf T}y(\mu)=x(\mu)^{\mathsf T}s(\mu)=n\mu.\] Consequently, primal and dual feasibility bracket the optimal value with gap \(n\mu\); thus \(\mu\le\varepsilon/n\) certifies a duality gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact ordinary central target has duality gap nμ, giving an immediate accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x(\mu)-b^{\mathsf T}y(\mu)=n\mu\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Central-Target Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordinary Path as Primal and Dual Barrier Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-optimization characterization of the ordinary standard-form primal-dual target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the ordinary central-path triple is equivalently characterized by \[x(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b,\,x>0}\left(c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\right)\] and \[y(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{c-A^{\mathsf T}y>0}\left(b^{\mathsf T}y+\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log(c-A^{\mathsf T}y)_i\right),\qquad s(\mu)=c-A^{\mathsf T}y(\mu).\] Their first-order conditions give \(s(\mu)=\mu X(\mu)^{-1}e\), equivalently \(X(\mu)s(\mu)=\mu e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary central target is simultaneously characterized by the primal and dual logarithmic-barrier optima.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual standard-form LPs are strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(\mu)\) and \(y(\mu)\) solve the displayed barrier problems and satisfy \(X(\mu)s(\mu)=\mu e\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Path as Primal and Dual Barrier Optima

children.title: Weighted-Path Targets
children.top_down_role: Target-following structures based on weighted barrier trajectories.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duality-gap certificate intrinsic to a fixed positive weighted target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a weighted target satisfying \(Xs=\mu w\), \[c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s=\mu e^{\mathsf T}w.\] Therefore \(\mu e^{\mathsf T}w\le\varepsilon\) certifies primal-dual gap at most \(\varepsilon\). Under the normalization \(e^{\mathsf T}w=n\), this reduces to the ordinary certificate \(n\mu\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted target has duality gap μ times the sum of its weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=\mu e^{\mathsf T}w\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Target Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization representation associated with fixed positive complementarity weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and \(\mu>0\). The weighted target is equivalently obtained from \[x_w(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b,\,x>0}\left(c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\log x_i\right).\] With equality multiplier \(-y_w(\mu)\), the first-order conditions define \(s_w(\mu)=c-A^{\mathsf T}y_w(\mu)>0\) and give \[s_{w,i}(\mu)=\frac{\mu w_i}{x_{w,i}(\mu)},\qquad X_w(\mu)s_w(\mu)=\mu w.\] Under full row rank and strict primal-dual feasibility, the weighted barrier minimizer and resulting target are unique. The objective and target equations depend on the weights through \(\mu w\), so positive rescaling of \(w\) is absorbed by inverse rescaling of \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive weight vector defines a weighted logarithmic barrier whose optimality conditions are the weighted complementarity equations; rescaling the weight vector only reparametrizes the target family.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal and dual LPs are strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_w(\mu)\) uniquely minimizes the weighted barrier objective and \(X_w(\mu)s_w(\mu)=\mu w\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Targets as Weighted-Barrier Optima
Weighted-Path Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-weighted primal-dual complementarity targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a weight vector \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). For \(\mu>0\), the weighted-path target is a strictly feasible triple satisfying \[Ax=b,\qquad A^Ty+s=c,\qquad Xs=\mu w,\qquad x>0,\ s>0.\] Thus the coordinate products satisfy \(x_is_i=\mu w_i\), rather than sharing one common value. Multiplying all weights by a positive scalar only reparametrizes the same target set: replacing \(w\) by \(\gamma w\) and \(\mu\) by \(\mu/\gamma\) leaves \(\mu w\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted target replaces equal complementarity products by coordinate products proportional to a fixed positive weight vector.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual LPs admit a strictly feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Xs=\mu w\), equivalently \(x_is_i=\mu w_i\) for every \(i\).
review_flags: The definition is standard but the supplied locators do not explicitly identify weighted central paths.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted complementarity definition is mathematically coherent and fits the container, but no specific authoritative locator supports this weighted-path convention.

children.title: Weight-Induced Trajectory Variants
children.top_down_role: Trajectory distinctions arising from alternative weighting choices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonproportional Weights Produce Distinct Target Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit standard-form LP separating two nonproportional weight rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{0:x_1+x_2=1,\ x>0\}\), whose dual equations are \(y+s_i=0\). For \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^2\), the weighted target equations give \[x_i=\frac{w_i}{w_1+w_2},\qquad y=-\mu(w_1+w_2),\qquad s_i=\mu(w_1+w_2).\] Hence nonproportional weights have different constant primal components and generate distinct primal-dual target trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-variable zero-cost LP explicitly shows that nonproportional positive weights can select different interior trajectories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=w/(w_1+w_2)\), so nonproportional weights yield distinct trajectories.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonproportional Weights Produce Distinct Target Trajectories

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weight-Ray Classification of Primal-Dual Target Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact classification of fixed-weight primal-dual target sets under positive rescaling of weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), let \(\mathcal T_w\) be the set of strictly feasible triples satisfying \(Xs=\mu w\) for some \(\mu>0\). For positive weights \(w,v\), \[\mathcal T_w\cap\mathcal T_v\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\gamma w\ \text{ for some }\gamma>0.\] In that case \(\mathcal T_v=\mathcal T_w\), with the parameter change \(\mu_v=\mu_w/\gamma\). Thus distinct positive weight rays generate disjoint primal-dual target trajectories whenever the corresponding targets exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two positive weight vectors generate the same primal-dual target trajectory exactly when they are positive scalar multiples.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T_w\) and \(\mathcal T_v\) use the same primal and dual feasibility equations.
The compared target sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_w=\mathcal T_v\) exactly when \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}w\); otherwise the sets are disjoint.

notation.meaning: Primal-dual target trajectory generated by the positive weight vector w.

review_flags: Classification concerns full primal-dual triples; projected primal trajectories can coincide under additional degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Ray Classification of Primal-Dual Target Trajectories
Weight-Induced Trajectory Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of weighted central trajectories on the chosen positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each fixed \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), define the weighted trajectory by the feasible equations and \(Xs=\mu w\) for \(\mu>0\). If their Jacobian is nonsingular, these equations locally determine a smooth trajectory \(z_w(\mu)\). Proportional weights generate the same geometric trajectory under reparametrization, whereas nonproportional weights generally generate distinct interior trajectories. For any such trajectory, the duality gap is \[c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts=\mu e^Tw,\] so it converges to zero as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weights select different interior trajectories; proportional weights merely reparametrize one trajectory, and every weighted trajectory has gap μ times the sum of its weights.
assumptions_latex: The defining Jacobian is nonsingular along the considered trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^Tx-b^Ty=\mu e^Tw\to0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
review_flags: A dedicated weighted-path source is needed for smoothness and trajectory classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gap identity follows from the displayed equations, but the smoothness and claim that nonproportional weights generally produce distinct trajectories require a dedicated source and a precise meaning of generally.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Target Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton centering on a primal objective-level slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a target value \(\tau\), consider the primal slice \(Ax=b\), \(c^Tx=\tau\), \(x>0\), and its logarithmic center, which maximizes \(\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\). From a strictly positive point, compute a Newton step for the equality-constrained barrier by solving \[X^{-2}\Delta x+A^T\Delta y+c\Delta\lambda=X^{-1}e,\qquad A\Delta x=b-Ax,\qquad c^T\Delta x=\tau-c^Tx.\] Choose a fraction-to-boundary step preserving \(x>0\), update \(x\), and repeat until the Newton decrement and slice residuals meet tolerance. An outer target method changes \(\tau\) toward the optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Center the positive primal feasible slice at a prescribed objective value using equality-constrained Newton steps, then advance the objective target.
assumptions_latex: The target slice contains a point \(x>0\).
The equality constraints defining the slice are independent.
The logarithmic-center problem attains its maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+ = x+\alpha\Delta x>0\), with \(Ax^+\) and \(c^Tx^+\) driven toward \(b\) and \(\tau\).

children.title: Coupled Primal–Dual Target Newton Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Primal–Dual Target Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton steps for simultaneous primal, dual, and complementarity targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given targets \(r_p^*\), \(r_d^*\), and \(q^*>0\), linearize the coupled equations \(Ax-b=r_p^*\), \(A^Ty+s-c=r_d^*\), and \(Xs=q^*\). At \((x,y,s)\) with \(x,s>0\), solve \[A\Delta x=r_p^*-(Ax-b),\qquad A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d^*-(A^Ty+s-c),\qquad S\Delta x+X\Delta s=q^*-Xs.\] Choose primal and dual fraction-to-boundary step lengths, update the triple, and repeat until the target residual is below tolerance. Central-path Newton methods result from \(r_p^*=r_d^*=0\) and \(q^*=\mu e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve one coupled Newton system that drives primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and coordinatewise complementarity toward prescribed targets while preserving positivity.
assumptions_latex: The coupled Newton matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Ax^+-b,\ A^Ty^++s^+-c,\ X^+s^+)\) is driven toward \((r_p^*,r_d^*,q^*)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Renegar Center-Method Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-target center method for strictly feasible standard-form LP slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an objective target \(\tau_0\) for which the slice \(F_{\tau_0}=\{x>0:Ax=b,\ c^Tx=\tau_0\}\) has a logarithmic center. At iteration \(k\), approximately maximize \(\sum_i\log x_i\) over \(F_{\tau_k}\) by damped Newton steps. Use the resulting center and its local barrier geometry to select a new target \(\tau_{k+1}<\tau_k\) whose slice remains nonempty and whose center lies within the prescribed Newton neighborhood. Repeat centering and target reduction; output the current feasible point when a certified objective bound or primal-dual gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately center an objective-level feasible slice and lower its objective target while keeping the next center within a controlled Newton neighborhood.

Each selected target slice has a logarithmic center.
A valid lower objective bound or dual certificate is available for stopping.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Update Path Following
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path following with Newton corrections restricted to selected coordinates or blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior primal-dual iterate, choose an index set \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) using a stated residual or complementarity rule. Compute a structured direction that enforces the linearized feasibility equations while imposing the target complementarity equation \(s_i\Delta x_i+x_i\Delta s_i=\mu_{k+1}-x_is_i\) for \(i\in I_k\); coordinates outside \(I_k\) are frozen or updated by the method's prescribed coupling rule. Choose a fraction-to-boundary step, update the selected block, and periodically perform a full correction so that the iterate remains in the chosen path neighborhood. Stop when feasibility residuals and the duality gap satisfy tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update only selected variable blocks toward their complementarity targets, preserve feasibility and positivity, and periodically use a full correction to maintain the path neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The block-selection rule guarantees every required coordinate is refreshed.
The structured Newton subproblem is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}>0\), \(s_{k+1}>0\), with selected products \(x_is_i\) moved toward \(\mu_{k+1}\).

children.title: Higher-Order Dikin-Direction Methods
children.top_down_role: Higher-order methods based on Dikin-type local geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Dikin-Direction Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Higher-order path steps expressed in log-barrier Dikin geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the barrier objective \(f_\mu(x)=c^Tx-\mu\sum_i\log x_i\) on \(Ax=b\), let \(H(x)=\mu X^{-2}\) define the Dikin norm. On the feasible tangent space \(A d=0\), form a degree-\(p\) local Taylor model of \(f_{\mu^+}(x+d)\), with \(p\ge3\), and compute a model-decreasing direction subject to \(\|d\|_x\le\rho<1\). Update \(x^+=x+d\), optionally recenter by a Newton step, and reduce \(\mu\) only when the prescribed neighborhood test holds. The Dikin-radius constraint guarantees \(x^+>0\); termination uses objective-gap or barrier-parameter tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a higher-order barrier model inside a Dikin ellipsoid, whose radius preserves positivity, and reduce the barrier parameter only after a neighborhood test.
assumptions_latex: The constrained Taylor-model subproblem has an accepted solution.

notation.meaning: Order of the local Taylor model.

review_flags: The title may denote a more specific higher-order Dikin construction than this generic local-model formulation.
A source is required for the precise direction and parameter-update rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement describes a generic higher-order Taylor model in barrier geometry, but no source connects it to the named Dikin-direction family. The inclusion of the barrier parameter in the stated norm also changes the usual Dikin-radius positivity condition and requires verification.

children.title: Higher-Order Log-Barrier Methods
children.top_down_role: Higher-order methods specialized to logarithmic-barrier trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Log-Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic higher-order primal log-barrier update; the precise advanced method family requires source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\), define \(F_\mu(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\). A higher-order log-barrier step of order \(p\ge 2\) selects \(d\) using derivatives \(\nabla^jF_\mu(x)\), \(1\le j\le p\), subject to \(Ad=0\) and \(x+d>0\); for example, it approximately minimizes \[T_p(d)=F_\mu(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{1}{j!}\nabla^jF_\mu(x)[d]^j\] within a prescribed trust region. After accepting \(x^+=x+d\), the method chooses \(0<\mu^+<\mu\) and repeats until the duality-gap and feasibility tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use derivatives beyond the Hessian to model the logarithmic-barrier objective, compute a feasible positive step, reduce the barrier parameter, and repeat to prescribed accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=x+d>0\) and \(Ax^+=b\), with the next subproblem using \(0<\mu^+<\mu\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual feasible and strictly feasible sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal-dual feasible set and its strictly feasible subset are \[\mathcal F=\{(x,\lambda,s):Ax=b,\ A^T\lambda+s=c,\ x\ge0,\ s\ge0\},\] \[\mathcal F^\circ=\{(x,\lambda,s):Ax=b,\ A^T\lambda+s=c,\ x>0,\ s>0\}.\] The inequalities are componentwise, and \(\lambda\) is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual feasible set consists of triples satisfying the primal and dual equality equations with nonnegative primal and slack variables. Its strictly feasible subset replaces nonnegativity by componentwise strict positivity; the equality multiplier remains unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad x,s\in\mathbb R^n,\quad \lambda,b\in\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F=\{(x,\lambda,s):Ax=b,\ A^T\lambda+s=c,\ (x,s)\ge0\},\qquad \mathcal F^\circ=\{(x,\lambda,s):Ax=b,\ A^T\lambda+s=c,\ (x,s)>0\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Strictly Feasible Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual strict-feasibility condition for a standard-form LP start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}.\] A known strictly feasible start is an explicitly available triple \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\) satisfying \[Ax^0=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0=c,\qquad x^0>0,\quad s^0>0.\] Its initial complementarity parameter is \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n>0\). No feasibility-restoration phase is required, although centrality may still need improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known strictly feasible start exactly satisfies both primal and dual equations and has every primal variable and slack strictly positive.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}.\] A triple \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) is an exact central start at parameter \(\mu_0>0\) if \[Ax^0=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0=c,\qquad x^0>0,\quad s^0>0,\qquad X^0S^0e=\mu_0e.\] Equivalently, \(x_i^0s_i^0=\mu_0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Thus the start lies exactly on the primal-dual central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact central start is strictly primal-dual feasible and has every initial complementary product equal to the same positive central-path parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}.\] Let \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) be strictly primal-dual feasible, define \(X^0=\operatorname{Diag}(x^0)\), \(S^0=\operatorname{Diag}(s^0)\), and set \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n\). For a prescribed \(0\le\theta<1\), the start belongs to the Euclidean neighborhood \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) when \[\lVert X^0S^0e-\mu_0e\rVert_2\le\theta\mu_0.\] The case \(\theta=0\) is exact centrality; positive \(\theta\) permits unequal complementary products subject to the displayed aggregate-deviation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly primal-dual feasible start is approximately central in the Euclidean neighborhood when the norm of its complementarity deviation is at most the prescribed fraction of its average complementarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Proximity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterization of initial central-path proximity by nested Euclidean neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a strictly feasible start, define its normalized initial proximity by \[\delta_0=\frac{\lVert X^0S^0e-\mu_0e\rVert_2}{\mu_0},\qquad \mu_0=\frac{(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0}{n}.\] Given thresholds \(0\le\theta_{\mathrm{near}}<\theta_{\mathrm{wide}}<1\), the exact, near-central, wide-neighborhood, and outside-neighborhood regimes are respectively \(\delta_0=0\), \(0<\delta_0\le\theta_{\mathrm{near}}\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{near}}<\delta_0\le\theta_{\mathrm{wide}}\), and \(\delta_0>\theta_{\mathrm{wide}}\). The numerical thresholds are algorithm parameters, not universal constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial proximity regimes classify a strictly feasible start by its normalized complementarity deviation relative to algorithm-specific near and wide thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_0\) assigns the start to exactly one of the four stated proximity regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Contraction Does Not Control Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing why a residual path requires a separate complementarity or centrality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(A=0\), \(b=0\), and \(c=1\) with the single primal variable \(x^k=1\) and dual slack \(s^k=1\) for every \(k\). Then \(Ax^k-b=0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k-c=0\) for every \(k\), while \((x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k=1\). Thus even identically zero feasibility residuals do not imply decreasing complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility residuals may vanish identically while complementarity stays positive, so a residual trajectory alone does not ensure optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p^k=r_d^k=0\ \text{for all }k,\qquad (x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k=1\not\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Contraction Does Not Control Complementarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic invariant underlying exact coupled residual trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_p=Ax-b\) and \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\). If \[A\Delta x=-r_p,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=-r_d,\] then a common step length \(\alpha\) gives \[r_p^+=(1-\alpha)r_p,\qquad r_d^+=(1-\alpha)r_d.\] Hence repeated common-step updates remain on rays through the initial residuals, with \(\rho_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common Newton step contracts both affine residuals by the same factor, placing accepted residuals on rays through their initial values.
assumptions_latex: The direction satisfies the displayed affine Newton equations
The same step length \(\alpha\) updates both affine equations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p^+=(1-\alpha)r_p,\qquad r_d^+=(1-\alpha)r_d.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Residual-Ray Recurrence
Residual-Path Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic infeasible path following with residuals constrained to a coupled contraction trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(x^0,s^0>0\), define \(r_p^0=b-Ax^0\) and \(r_d^0=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^0-s^0\). A residual-path method chooses decreasing \(\rho_k\downarrow0\) and \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), and computes interior iterates satisfying, exactly or within stated neighborhood tolerances, \[b-Ax^k=\rho_kr_p^0,\qquad c-A^{\mathsf T}y^k-s^k=\rho_kr_d^0,\qquad X^kS^ke\approx\mu_ke.\] Each update is obtained from the Newton linearization of these three equations, with a step length preserving \(x^{k+1},s^{k+1}>0\). The method stops when both residual norms and \((x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k\) meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method contracts primal and dual residuals along a prescribed path while simultaneously reducing complementarity and retaining positivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p^k\to0\), \(r_d^k\to0\), and \((x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k\to0\) when the prescribed trajectory is followed.

8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\},\] let \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\), with \(x,s>0\). The affine predictor solves \[A\Delta x^{\rm aff}=r_p,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\rm aff}+\Delta s^{\rm aff}=r_d,\qquad S\Delta x^{\rm aff}+X\Delta s^{\rm aff}=-XSe.\] Let \(\alpha_p^{\rm aff}\) and \(\alpha_d^{\rm aff}\) be the largest step lengths in \([0,1]\) for which \(x+\alpha_p^{\rm aff}\Delta x^{\rm aff}\ge0\) and \(s+\alpha_d^{\rm aff}\Delta s^{\rm aff}\ge0\), and define \[\mu_{\rm aff}=\frac{(x+\alpha_p^{\rm aff}\Delta x^{\rm aff})^{\mathsf T}(s+\alpha_d^{\rm aff}\Delta s^{\rm aff})}{n},\qquad \sigma=\left(\frac{\mu_{\rm aff}}{\mu}\right)^3.\] The combined predictor-corrector direction solves the same first two Newton equations and uses the complementarity right-hand side \[-XSe+\sigma\mu e-\Delta X^{\rm aff}\Delta S^{\rm aff}e.\] Damped primal and dual step lengths are then chosen strictly below their positivity limits, and \((x,y,s)\) is updated until the prescribed residual and duality-gap tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method computes an infeasible affine predictor, uses its positivity-limited complementarity to choose a centering parameter, adds the second-order predictor correction, and takes damped positive primal and dual steps until residual and gap tolerances are met.

children.title: Infeasible Warm-Start Methods
children.top_down_role: Path restoration from interior points inherited from related LP instances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positivity Alone Does Not Validate an Interior-Point Warm Start
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary distinction between a positive inherited point and a useful path-following warm start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inherited estimate \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\), conditions \(\bar x>0\) and \(\bar s>0\) alone imply neither small residuals \(b-A\bar x\), \(c-A^{\mathsf T}\bar y-\bar s\) nor membership in a prescribed central-path neighborhood. Positivity shifts alone therefore imply no restoration guarantee or iteration advantage over generic infeasible initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive inherited point can remain highly infeasible or noncentral, so positivity alone does not establish a useful warm start.
assumptions_latex: No residual or central-neighborhood bound is imposed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x>0,\ \bar s>0\ \not\Longrightarrow\ \text{small residuals, centrality, or a warm-start complexity improvement}.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Alone Does Not Validate an Interior-Point Warm Start
Infeasible Warm-Start Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic restoration path from a positive solution estimate inherited from a related LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a related-instance estimate \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\), first enforce strict positivity by \(x^0=\bar x+\delta_xe>0\) and \(s^0=\bar s+\delta_se>0\), leaving \(y^0=\bar y\). Form \(r_p^0=b-Ax^0\), \(r_d^0=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^0-s^0\), and \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n\). Apply damped primal-dual Newton steps targeting \[r_p^k=\rho_kr_p^0,\qquad r_d^k=\rho_kr_d^0,\qquad X^kS^ke\approx\mu_ke,\] with \(\rho_k,\mu_k\downarrow0\). Output the restored point once it enters the path-following neighborhood and satisfies the requested residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift an inherited estimate into the positive orthant, then restore feasibility and centrality along contracting residual and complementarity targets.
assumptions_latex: A related LP supplies \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is positive, approximately primal-dual feasible, and lies in the chosen central neighborhood.

children.title: Classical Self-Dual Embedding
children.top_down_role: Self-dual augmentation of the primal-dual LP pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Self-Dual Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition of a self-dual augmentation used to initialize and solve an LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual LP pair \((P,D)\), a classical self-dual embedding is an augmented linear program \(E(P,D)\) together with a fixed involution \(J\) such that the dual of \(E(P,D)\), after applying \(J\), has the same constraint matrix, right-hand side, objective, and cone as \(E(P,D)\). The embedding must also provide a projection \(\pi\) for which every embedded optimal solution with positive normalization component maps under \(\pi\) to a primal-dual optimal solution of \((P,D)\). Auxiliary variables may encode initialization and the primal-dual gap but do not alter the projected optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classical self-dual embedding augments an LP so that the embedded primal and dual coincide and normalized embedded solutions recover original primal-dual optima.
assumptions_latex: The embedding specifies its involution \(J\) and recovery map \(\pi\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J(E(P,D)^*)=E(P,D)\), and normalized embedded optima project to optima of \((P,D)\).

notation.meaning: Recovery projection to the original variables

children.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous embedded paths supporting unified outcome recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard homogeneous embedding of a primal-dual LP with normalization variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D:\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), the homogeneous self-dual system is \[Ax-b\tau=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\tau=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x+\kappa=0,\] with \(x,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\). If \(\tau>0\), then \((x/\tau,y/\tau,s/\tau)\) is primal-dual feasible and its gap is \(\kappa/\tau\); if additionally \(\kappa=0\), it is optimal. A terminal solution with \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) may instead yield an infeasibility certificate, subject to the signs of its primal or dual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization introduces scale and gap variables, enabling one embedded system to recover optimal solutions or, at zero scale, infeasibility certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau>0\) permits recovery by scaling; \(\tau=0<\kappa\) is the certificate-producing regime.

children.title: Artificial-Start Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Embedded formulations constructed to provide an immediate interior start.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Start Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding class whose auxiliary variables manufacture a known strictly interior initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An artificial-start embedding of an LP \(P\) is an augmented primal-dual formulation \(E(P;z^0)\) containing auxiliary variables and residual offsets chosen from a prescribed \(z^0\) so that \(z^0\) satisfies every embedded equality and all embedded inequality variables are strictly positive. The formulation must include a recovery rule: when its artificial variables vanish and its normalization variable is positive, scaling and projecting the remaining variables gives a feasible primal-dual pair for \(P\); zero complementarity then gives an optimal pair. Thus initialization is immediate in the embedding even when no feasible start for \(P\) is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables and offsets create an immediately known interior point, while vanishing artificial variables permit recovery of a solution to the original LP.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a specified primal-dual LP pair
The augmented formulation supplies a strictly positive prescribed point \(z^0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^0\in\operatorname{int}E(P;z^0)\), and a normalized terminal point with zero artificial variables projects to a solution of \(P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Start Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence from feasible interior iterates with uniform complementarity contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal-dual LP having an optimal solution. Let \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) satisfy \[Ax^k=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k=c,\qquad x^k>0,\quad s^k>0\] for every \(k\), and define \(\mu_k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k/n\). If there exists \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-\eta)\mu_k\) for all \(k\), then \(\mu_k\to0\) and \[c^{\mathsf T}x^k-b^{\mathsf T}y^k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k=n\mu_k\to0.\] Consequently the primal and dual objective values converge to the common optimum, and every finite cluster point is primal-dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly feasible primal-dual iterates whose complementarity contracts uniformly have vanishing duality gap; their objective values converge globally, and every cluster point is optimal.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual LP has an optimal solution
Every iterate is strictly primal-dual feasible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_k\to0\), both objective sequences converge to the optimal value, and every cluster point is optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A residual-and-gap convergence theorem for bounded infeasible-start primal-dual LP iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\). Let \(x^k,s^k>0\), and suppose \(\{(x^k,y^k,s^k)\}\) is bounded, \(Ax^k-b\to0\), \(A^Ty^k+s^k-c\to0\), and \((x^k)^Ts^k\to0\). Then the distance from \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) to the primal-dual solution set tends to zero. In particular, every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal and satisfies complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded positive iterates whose primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity gap vanish approach the primal-dual solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k,s^k>0\) and the iterate sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}((x^k,y^k,s^k),\mathcal S)\to0\), where \(\mathcal S\) is the primal-dual solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Convergence for Bounded Infeasible Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value consequence of simultaneous residual and complementarity convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the seed hypotheses, define \(r_p^k=Ax^k-b\) and \(r_d^k=A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k-c\). Then \[c^{\mathsf T}x^k-b^{\mathsf T}y^k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k-(x^k)^{\mathsf T}r_d^k+(y^k)^{\mathsf T}r_p^k\to0.\] Since the bounded sequence approaches the primal-dual solution set, \(c^{\mathsf T}x^k\to v^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y^k\to v^*\), where \(v^*\) is the common optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded infeasible iterates with vanishing residuals and complementarity have vanishing objective gap, and both objectives converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{\mathsf T}x^k-b^{\mathsf T}y^k\to0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x^k\to v^*,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y^k\to v^*.

children.title: Limit-Point Convergence
children.top_down_role: Optimality and complementarity of accumulation points.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality of finite accumulation points under residual and complementarity convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard primal-dual LP pair, let \((x^{k_j},y^{k_j},s^{k_j})\to(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) along a subsequence with \(x^k,s^k\ge0\). If \(Ax^k-b\to0\), \(A^Ty^k+s^k-c\to0\), and \((x^k)^Ts^k\to0\), then \(A\bar x=b\), \(A^T\bar y+\bar s=c\), \(\bar x,\bar s\ge0\), and \(\bar x^T\bar s=0\). Hence \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) is primal-dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite cluster point is primal-dual optimal when feasibility residuals and the nonnegative complementarity gap vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k,s^k\ge0\) and a finite convergent subsequence exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\in\mathcal S\).

notation.meaning: A finite accumulation point of the iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A uniqueness condition upgrading convergence to the solution set into convergence of all iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\) be a bounded primal-dual sequence satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(z^k,\mathcal S)\to0\), where \(\mathcal S\) is the primal-dual solution set. If \(\mathcal S=\{z^*\}\) is a singleton, then the complete sequence converges: \(z^k\to z^*\). Without uniqueness, optimality of every accumulation point alone does not imply convergence of the full sequence, since distinct subsequences may approach distinct points of \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approach to a singleton solution set forces the entire bounded sequence to converge; optimal cluster points alone do not.

children.title: Feasible Complementarity-Gap Criteria

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Complementarity-Gap Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact identity and optimality criterion for primal-dual feasible LP points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), \(Ax=b\), and \(A^Ty+s=c\), then the primal-dual objective gap obeys \[c^Tx-b^Ty=x^T(c-A^Ty)=x^Ts\ge0.\] Consequently, a feasible triple is primal-dual optimal if and only if \(x^Ts=0\). For a sequence of exactly feasible triples, \((x^k)^Ts^k\to0\) is equivalent to the primal and dual objective values approaching one another; every finite accumulation point is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At feasible primal-dual points, the objective gap equals complementarity, and zero gap exactly characterizes optimality. For an exactly feasible sequence, vanishing complementarity is equivalent to convergence of the primal and dual objective values to one another, and every finite accumulation point is optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\ge0\), with optimality equivalent to \(x^Ts=0\).

children.title: Residual–Gap Compatibility Criteria
children.top_down_role: Joint feasibility and complementarity criteria for infeasible-start methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Gap Compatibility Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint asymptotic feasibility and complementarity predicate for infeasible-start LP sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative primal-dual iterates \(x^k,s^k\ge0\), define \(r_p^k=Ax^k-b\), \(r_d^k=A^Ty^k+s^k-c\), and \(\mu_k=(x^k)^Ts^k/n\). The residual-gap compatibility criterion is \[\|r_p^k\|\to0,\qquad \|r_d^k\|\to0,\qquad \mu_k\to0.\] Any finite accumulation point of a sequence satisfying this criterion is primal feasible, dual feasible, and complementary, and therefore solves the primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal residual, dual residual, and normalized complementarity must vanish jointly to recover optimality from infeasible-start iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite accumulation point belongs to the primal-dual solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual–Gap Compatibility Does Not Ensure Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct boundary, but canonically owned by the Sequence-to-Solution Recovery Criteria sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The limits \(\|Ax^k-b\|\to0\), \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k-c\|\to0\), and \((x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k\to0\), with \(x^k,s^k\ge0\), do not alone imply boundedness, existence of a finite accumulation point, or convergence of the full sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-gap compatibility certifies finite cluster points but does not itself provide sequence compactness or convergence.
assumptions_latex: Both feasibility residuals and complementarity vanish
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Compatibility}\not\Longrightarrow\text{boundedness or full-sequence convergence}.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Iterate Sequences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every bounded sequence \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\) in finite-dimensional primal-dual space has a convergent subsequence. If additionally \(x^k,s^k\ge0\) and the primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity gap all converge to zero, then each convergent subsequence has a primal-dual optimal limit. Thus boundedness guarantees existence of at least one recoverable optimal cluster point.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Point Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A limit triple certifies recovery when residuals and complementarity vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^{k_j},y^{k_j},s^{k_j})\to(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\), with \(x^k,s^k\ge0\). The computable quantities \(Ax^{k_j}-b\), \(A^Ty^{k_j}+s^{k_j}-c\), and \((x^{k_j})^Ts^{k_j}\) form a solution-recovery certificate when all tend to zero. Continuity yields primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and \(\bar x^T\bar s=0\); weak duality then certifies that \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) is primal-dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite cluster point is certified optimal by vanishing primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Sequence Recovery Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing residuals and complementarity need not produce a finite cluster point without boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{0:x_1=1,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(A=(1,0)\), \(b=1\), and \(c=(0,0)\). Set \(x^k=(1,k)\), \(y^k=-1/k\), and \(s^k=(1/k,1/k^2)>0\). Then \(Ax^k-b=0\), \(A^Ty^k+s^k-c=(0,1/k^2)\to0\), and \((x^k)^Ts^k=2/k\to0\). Nevertheless, \(\|x^k\|\to\infty\), so the sequence has no finite cluster point from which a solution can be recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals and complementarity may vanish along an unbounded sequence having no finite recoverable cluster point.
assumptions_latex: The LP and sequence are defined as displayed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^k\|\to\infty\) despite \(r_p^k\to0\), \(r_d^k\to0\), and \((x^k)^Ts^k\to0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Convergence of Fixed-Parameter Newton Centering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence of full Newton iterations for the fixed positive primal-dual barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_\mu(x,y,s)=(Ax-b,A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c,XSe-\mu e), with \mu>0. If F_\mu(z_\mu)=0, x_\mu>0, s_\mu>0, F_\mu'(z_\mu) is nonsingular, and F_\mu' is locally Lipschitz, then for every sufficiently close z^0 the full Newton iteration z^{k+1}=z^k-F_\mu'(z^k)^{-1}F_\mu(z^k) is well defined and satisfies \|z^{k+1}-z_\mu\|\le C\|z^k-z_\mu\|^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full Newton centering converges locally quadratically to a regular positive fixed-parameter barrier center.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\mu'\) is locally Lipschitz and \(z^0\) is sufficiently close to \(z_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z^{k+1}-z_\mu\|\le C\|z^k-z_\mu\|^2\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from the components of x and s.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Convergence of Fixed-Parameter Newton Centering
Local Quadratic Centering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton quadratic convergence for a fixed positive barrier parameter near its center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\mu>0\) and define the primal-dual centering equations \(F_\mu(x,y,s)=(Ax-b,\ A^Ty+s-c,\ XSe-\mu e)=0\). Suppose \(z_\mu=(x_\mu,y_\mu,s_\mu)\) has \(x_\mu,s_\mu>0\), the Jacobian \(F_\mu'(z_\mu)\) is nonsingular, and \(F_\mu'\) is Lipschitz near \(z_\mu\). Then undamped Newton centering, \(z^{k+1}=z^k-F_\mu'(z^k)^{-1}F_\mu(z^k)\), is well defined for sufficiently close \(z^0\) and satisfies \(\|z^{k+1}-z_\mu\|\le C\|z^k-z_\mu\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular positive barrier center, full Newton centering converges quadratically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z^{k+1}-z_\mu\|\le C\|z^k-z_\mu\|^2\) locally.

children.title: Predictor-Corrector Superlinear Convergence
children.top_down_role: Superlinear local convergence families for predictor-corrector methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictor-Corrector Superlinear Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional superlinear rate for full-step predictor-corrector iterations near a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(z)=0\) denote a locally smooth primal-dual optimality system with solution \(z^*\), nonsingular \(F'(z^*)\), and locally Lipschitz Jacobian. Suppose a predictor-corrector step \(d^k\) is eventually accepted with unit length and satisfies \[F'(z^k)d^k=-F(z^k)+q^k,\qquad \|q^k\|=o(\|F(z^k)\|).\] If \(z^k\to z^*\), then \(\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|/\|z^k-z^*\|\to0\); hence the local convergence is Q-superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full predictor-corrector step with asymptotically negligible linearization error converges Q-superlinearly near a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \frac{\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|}{\|z^k-z^*\|}\to0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Quadratic Path Following
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact-Newton rate family whose order can approach two along the barrier path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(z^*)=0\), with \(F'(z^*)\) nonsingular and locally Lipschitz. Suppose full path-following steps satisfy \[F'(z^k)(z^{k+1}-z^k)=-F(z^k)+q^k,\qquad \|q^k\|\le C\|F(z^k)\|^{1+\theta},\] for some \(0<\theta<1\). For iterates sufficiently near \(z^*\), \(\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|=O(\|z^k-z^*\|^{1+\theta})\). Thus choosing \(\theta\) arbitrarily close to one yields convergence order arbitrarily close to quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlling correction error to power one plus theta gives local order one plus theta, approaching quadratic as theta approaches one.
assumptions_latex: Full steps are taken sufficiently near \(z^*\).

notation.meaning: Rate parameter between zero and one.

children.title: Higher-Order Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local rate families associated with higher-order trajectory models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate classification for higher-order local primal-dual iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\to z^*\) and \(q>1\). The sequence has Q-order at least \(q\) if there are \(C>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \[\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z^k-z^*\|^q\qquad(k\ge k_0).\] In this leaf, higher-order convergence means \(q>2\). Such a rate satisfies \(\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z^k-z^*\|^2)\), and therefore is Q-superquadratic, Q-quadratic, and Q-superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-order local convergence has an error exponent greater than two and consequently is superquadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Q-Convergence
Higher-Order Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional local order from higher-degree trajectory models and sufficiently accurate corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(p+1\) times continuously differentiable near \(z^*\), where \(F(z^*)=0\) and \(F'(z^*)\) is nonsingular. Suppose a degree-\(p\) local trajectory model and correction produce iterates satisfying \(\|F(z^{k+1})\|\le C\|F(z^k)\|^{p+1}\). Then, for iterates sufficiently near \(z^*\), \[\|z^{k+1}-z^*\|\le C'\|z^k-z^*\|^{p+1}.\] Hence the resulting local convergence has Q-order at least \(p+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular higher-degree trajectory correction with residual order p plus one yields local convergence of at least that order.

notation.meaning: Degree of the local trajectory model.
Regular solution of the residual equations.
