children.title: Rank-Deficient LP Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Redundant equality systems producing singular path representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient LP Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity caused by redundant equality rows in primal-dual path equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a strictly positive primal-dual point, elimination in the Newton equations produces the normal-equation matrix \(M=A X S^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), where \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). Because \(X S^{-1}\) is positive definite, \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\). Hence if \(A\) lacks full row rank, then \(M\) is singular even though the represented feasible set may be regular; redundant equalities must be removed or the Newton system solved with rank-revealing linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equality rows make the primal-dual normal equations singular, independently of strict positivity of the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: The Newton system is reduced to the displayed normal-equation form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\Longrightarrow AXS^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is singular.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Left-null test distinguishing harmless redundancy from an inconsistent LP description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the equality system \(Ax=b\) is consistent if and only if \[z^{\mathsf T}b=0\quad\text{for every }z\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T}).\] Thus a vector \(z\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}z=0\) and \(z^{\mathsf T}b\ne0\) certifies inconsistency, whereas left-null vectors orthogonal to \(b\) represent compatible equality dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null equality dependency is compatible exactly when it is also obeyed by the right-hand side; otherwise it certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\text{ is consistent}\iff z^{\mathsf T}b=0\ \forall z\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Boundary for Redundant Equalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent central-path representation after removal of consistent redundant equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r<m\), and suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Choose \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\) such that \(\widehat A=RA\) has rank \(r\) and the rows of \(\widehat A\) span the row space of \(A\); set \(\widehat b=Rb\). Then \[\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:\widehat A x=\widehat b\}.\] Hence the primal logarithmic-barrier subproblems and primal central path are unchanged. In the unreduced dual representation, multipliers are defined only modulo \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\): if \(z\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), then \(y\) and \(y+z\) produce the same slack, and consistency implies \(z^{\mathsf T}b=0\), so they also have the same dual objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible redundant equalities can be replaced by a full-row-rank system without changing the primal barrier path; unreduced equality multipliers remain nonunique along the left null space.
assumptions_latex: The rows of \(RA\) form a basis of the row space of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:RAx=Rb\}\), while equivalent dual multipliers differ by vectors in \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Map producing an independent basis of the equality row space.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Row-Rank Reduction and Multiplier Quotient

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Solution Approach
children.top_down_role: Path regimes with deteriorating scaling near the solution boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Solution Approach
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling deterioration along a strictly complementary central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along the exact central path, \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\). Suppose its limit is strictly complementary and has indices \(i,j\) with \(x_i^*>0,\ s_i^*=0\) and \(x_j^*=0,\ s_j^*>0\). Then \(x_i(\mu)/s_i(\mu)=\Theta(\mu^{-1})\), while \(x_j(\mu)/s_j(\mu)=\Theta(\mu)\). Consequently, the condition number of the diagonal scaling \(X(\mu)S(\mu)^{-1}\) is at least of order \(\mu^{-2}\), exposing increasing numerical sensitivity as the solution boundary is approached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity forces primal-dual scaling ratios onto reciprocal scales, so diagonal scaling becomes increasingly ill-conditioned as the barrier parameter vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The exact central-path equations hold for \(\mu>0\).
The limiting solution is strictly complementary and contains both a primal-positive and a slack-positive coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(X(\mu)S(\mu)^{-1})=\Omega(\mu^{-2})\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

children.title: Gap-Residual Mismatch Boundary
children.top_down_role: The failure of complementarity reduction alone to certify feasibility.

children.title: Small-Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Iterate regimes exhibiting low complementarity or primal-dual gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Gap Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized stopping regime based solely on primal-dual objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an approximate primal-dual triple \((x,y,s)\) with \(x,s\ge0\), define the normalized gap \(\eta_g=|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|/(1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|)\). Given a tolerance \(\varepsilon_g>0\), the small-gap regime is the predicate \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\). This condition measures approximate objective agreement only; without separate bounds on primal and dual residuals, it neither asserts approximate feasibility nor certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized primal-dual objective gap is small, but this condition alone says nothing about feasibility residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
The primal and dual objectives are finite at the reported vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\) defines small gap but does not alone imply approximate optimality.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

review_flags: Normalization convention is local to this record.

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

children.title: Large-Residual Regime
children.top_down_role: Iterate regimes retaining substantial feasibility residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Residual Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized feasibility-residual boundary for an approximate primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,s\ge0\), define \(\eta_p=\|Ax-b\|_2/(1+\|b\|_2)\) and \(\eta_d=\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|_2/(1+\|c\|_2)\). Given \(\varepsilon_f>0\), the large-residual regime is \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}>\varepsilon_f\). A point in this regime fails the prescribed primal-dual feasibility test regardless of the size of its objective gap or complementarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At least one normalized primal or dual feasibility residual exceeds tolerance, so the point fails the feasibility test.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
Residuals are measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}>\varepsilon_f\Longrightarrow\) the reported point is not certified approximately feasible at tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\).

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

review_flags: Normalization convention is local to this record.

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

children.title: Gap–Residual Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Progress-measure configurations combining a small gap with large residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Residual Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of gap-only stopping when feasibility residuals remain large.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\eta_g=|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|/(1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|)\), \(\eta_p=\|Ax-b\|_2/(1+\|b\|_2)\), and \(\eta_d=\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|_2/(1+\|c\|_2)\). A gap-residual mismatch at tolerances \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_f)\) occurs when \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\) but \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}>\varepsilon_f\). The first inequality can hold through cancellation or near agreement of two objectives evaluated at infeasible vectors. Therefore, a gap-only termination rule can accept a point that fails primal or dual feasibility and does not constitute an approximate optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small objective gap can coexist with an excessive feasibility residual, making gap-only termination invalid.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
The normalized quantities use the local conventions displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}>\varepsilon_f\Longrightarrow\) no gap-only optimality certificate is valid.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

review_flags: Normalization convention is inherited from prerequisite records.

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

assumptions_latex: The local normalized residual and gap conventions are those of the immutable seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g=0\le\varepsilon_g\quad\text{and}\quad\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}=1/2>\varepsilon_f.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit zero-gap instance exhibiting the locally defined gap-residual mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar standard-form data \(A=[1]\), \(b=1\), and \(c=0\), take \(x=0\), \(y=0\), and \(s=0\). Then \(x,s\ge0\), the primal and dual candidate objective values are both zero, and the dual residual is zero. Under the local normalizations, \(\eta_g=0\), \(\eta_d=0\), and \(\eta_p=|Ax-b|/(1+|b|)=1/2\). Consequently this tuple lies in the mismatch regime for every \(\varepsilon_g>0\) and every \(0<\varepsilon_f<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable candidate can have exactly zero primal-dual objective gap and zero dual residual while retaining a fixed, excessive primal feasibility residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Large-Residual Family

children.title: Feasibility-Certification Failure
children.top_down_role: Limits on feasibility conclusions drawn from complementarity reduction alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Certification Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating objective agreement from a valid approximate optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-form primal-dual pair, define \(\eta_p=\|Ax-b\|_2/(1+\|b\|_2)\), \(\eta_d=\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|_2/(1+\|c\|_2)\), and \(\eta_g=|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|/(1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|)\). An approximate optimality certificate at tolerances \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_g)\) requires \(x,s\ge0\), \(\eta_p\le\varepsilon_f\), \(\eta_d\le\varepsilon_f\), and \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\). If either feasibility inequality fails, then the tuple does not certify approximate primal-dual optimality, even when its objective gap or complementarity is arbitrarily small. Accordingly, status reporting must retain feasibility residuals as independent acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small gap or complementarity cannot certify approximate optimality when either primal or dual feasibility test fails.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
The normalized quantities use the local conventions displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_p>\varepsilon_f\) or \(\eta_d>\varepsilon_f\Longrightarrow\) failure of approximate-optimality certification.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

review_flags: Tolerance and normalization conventions are local to this shard.

children.title: Unbounded-Sequence Recovery Boundary
children.top_down_role: The compactness boundary for recovering solutions from vanishing measures.

assumptions_latex: The zero-cost conclusion additionally assumes \(c^{\mathsf T}x^k/\|x^k\|_2\to0\), which holds when \(|c^{\mathsf T}x^k|\) is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^{k_j}\to d\Longrightarrow d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\setminus\{0\};\qquad \frac{c^{\mathsf T}x^{k_j}}{\|x^{k_j}\|_2}\to0\Longrightarrow c^{\mathsf T}d=0.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional information recoverable after finite solution recovery fails through loss of compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and let \(x^k\in P\) satisfy \(\|x^k\|_2\to\infty\). Set \(d^k=x^k/\|x^k\|_2\). The sequence \(d^k\) has a convergent subsequence, and every limit \(d^{k_j}\to d\) satisfies \(d\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\|d\|_2=1\); hence \(d\) is a nonzero recession direction of \(P\). If additionally \(c^{\mathsf T}x^k/\|x^k\|_2\to0\), in particular if \(|c^{\mathsf T}x^k|\) is uniformly bounded, then every such limit satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\). Thus normalization can recover a zero-cost recession direction even when the original sequence has no finite solution subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unbounded feasible sequence has normalized subsequences converging to nonzero recession directions; objective values bounded in absolute value force the recovered directions to have zero objective slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Escape Directions from Unbounded Feasible Sequences
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Escape Directions from Unbounded Feasible Sequences
Unbounded-Sequence Recovery Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of solution recovery without boundedness of an approximate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min 0\) subject to \(x_1=1\) and \(x_1,x_2\ge0\). The sequence \(x^k=(1,k)\) is exactly feasible and optimal, so its aggregate feasibility residual \(r_k\) and objective gap \(g_k\) satisfy \(r_k=g_k=0\) for every \(k\). Nevertheless, \(\|x^k\|_2\to\infty\), and no subsequence converges to a finite solution. Thus vanishing residuals and gaps recover a solution through subsequential limits only when the approximate sequence is bounded or another compactness mechanism is available. Normalization of an unbounded sequence may instead reveal a recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact feasibility and zero gap do not ensure a recoverable finite limit when the reported solution sequence is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: Convergence and boundedness are taken in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k\to0\) and \(g_k\to0\) do not imply existence of a convergent solution subsequence without boundedness.

children.top_down_role: The effect of inaccurate Newton directions on centrality and progress guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Direction Neighborhood Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness boundary for the Euclidean central-path neighborhood under additive primal-dual direction errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge 1\), let \(x,s,\Delta x,\Delta s,u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(e\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be the all-ones vector, and set \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(P=I-ee^{\mathsf T}/n\). For \(0<\alpha\le 1\), define the exact trial complementarity vector \(w_*=(x+\alpha\Delta x)\circ(s+\alpha\Delta s)\), its mean \(\mu_*=e^{\mathsf T}w_*/n\), and its centrality margin \(m=\theta\mu_*-\lVert Pw_*\rVert_2\). The trial using the perturbed directions \(\Delta x+u\) and \(\Delta s+v\) has complementarity vector \(w_*+q\), where
\[
q=\alpha(Su+Xv)+\alpha^2(\Delta x\circ v+\Delta s\circ u+u\circ v).
\]
If the exact and perturbed trial points are positive, \(m\ge 0\), and
\[
\lVert Pq\rVert_2+\frac{\theta}{n}\lvert e^{\mathsf T}q\rvert\le m,
\]
then the perturbed trial belongs to
\[
N_2(\theta)=\left\{(y,z)\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\times\mathbb{R}_{++}^n:\left\lVert \operatorname{Diag}(y)\operatorname{Diag}(z)e-\mu(y,z)e\right\rVert_2\le\theta\mu(y,z)\right\},
\]
where \(\mu(y,z)=y^{\mathsf T}z/n\). If the error budget is exceeded, this sufficient margin argument no longer guarantees neighborhood membership or any progress result that assumes it; the perturbed point may nevertheless remain in the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive inexact Newton trial remains in the Euclidean central neighborhood if its projected complementarity perturbation plus its worst-case mean-gap perturbation does not exceed the exact trial's centrality margin. Exceeding this sufficient budget removes the guarantee but does not prove that neighborhood membership fails.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s,\Delta x,\Delta s,u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(u\) and \(v\) the additive direction errors.
The exact trial point \((x+\alpha\Delta x,s+\alpha\Delta s)\) and the perturbed trial point \((x+\alpha(\Delta x+u),s+\alpha(\Delta s+v))\) are componentwise positive.
The exact trial has nonnegative centrality margin \(m=\theta\mu_*-\lVert Pw_*\rVert_2\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\lVert Pq\rVert_2+\theta\lvert e^{\mathsf T}q\rvert/n\le m\) implies that the perturbed trial lies in \(N_2(\theta)\); if it is violated, this sufficient bound supplies no neighborhood-membership guarantee.

notation.meaning: Additive errors in the primal and dual Newton directions.
The orthogonal projector onto the subspace perpendicular to the all-ones vector.
The complementarity-vector perturbation caused by the direction errors.
The exact trial's margin to the boundary of \(N_2(\theta)\).

notation.meaning: Additive primal and dual direction errors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positivity obstruction for absolute inexact-direction tolerances over the entire strict interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\alpha>0\) and any absolute error allowance \(\delta>0\). In one dimension choose \(x=s=\varepsilon>0\), exact directions \(\Delta x=\Delta s=0\), and additive errors \(u=-2\varepsilon/\alpha\), \(v=0\), where \(0<\varepsilon<\alpha\delta/2\). Then \(\|(u,v)\|_2=2\varepsilon/\alpha<\delta\), but the inexact primal trial is \(x+\alpha(\Delta x+u)=-\varepsilon<0\). Therefore no positive uniform bound on an unscaled absolute direction-error norm preserves positivity, and hence central-neighborhood membership, over all strictly positive iterates. Error control must instead scale with distance to the orthant boundary or be combined with step shortening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small absolute direction errors can cross the positivity boundary when an iterate component is sufficiently small, so no uniform unscaled error tolerance protects the central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Absolute Direction-Error Tolerance

children.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Numerical ambiguity among optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, and severe ill-conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for classifying an LP when its data are known only within a finite error radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent a scalar standard-form LP by data \(d=(a,b,c)\) and the problem
\[
\inf\{cx:ax=b,\ x\ge0\}.
\]
If measured data \(\widehat d\) are known only to satisfy \(\lVert d-\widehat d\rVert_\infty\le\eta\), a unique exact status is certifiable from the measurement only if every LP in that uncertainty ball has the same status. This condition fails at \(\widehat d=(0,0,0)\) for every \(\eta>0\): for any \(0<\varepsilon\le\eta\), the data \((0,0,\varepsilon)\) define an LP with a finite optimum, \((0,0,-\varepsilon)\) define an unbounded LP, and \((0,\varepsilon,0)\) define an infeasible LP. Thus arbitrarily small data uncertainty can make optimality, infeasibility, and unboundedness numerically indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-precision status certificate is impossible when the data uncertainty ball intersects different exact-status regions; a one-variable LP exhibits this ambiguity at arbitrarily small radii.
assumptions_latex: The LP data are observed with absolute componentwise error at most \(\eta>0\).
Status means finite optimum, primal infeasibility, or primal unboundedness in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\widehat d=(0,0,0)\), no positive uncertainty radius \(\eta\) determines a unique LP status without additional information or stronger error bounds.

notation.meaning: Scalar constraint coefficient, right-hand side, and objective coefficient.
